mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLE 250d or 300d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the GLE 250d costs £2,500-£3,200 supply-only; a rebuilt OM654 engine for the GLE 300d costs £2,800-£3,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes GLE 250d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. If ignored, it can lead to misfires, cam/crank correlation codes, and catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLE 300d engine (OM654) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654 is a modern, efficient diesel with strong performance. However, it has a known EGR system weakness - clogging and cooler failures that can occur from 50,000 miles. With proper maintenance and EGR attention, these engines exceed 150,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLE 250d and 300d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. The OM654 is too new for definitive long-term data, but early indications suggest similar longevity with proper maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLE 250d or 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLE is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £2,500-£3,200 - far less than replacing a £12,000-£20,000 vehicle. The GLE 300d's higher value (£25,000-£45,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLE 250d or 300d need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM651 requires approximately 6.5 litres; the OM654 requires approximately 7 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 250d/300d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLE 250d launched with the W166 generation in 2015 as the entry-level diesel, powered by the OM651 2.1-litre twin-turbo four-cylinder producing 204hp. In 2019, the W167 GLE 300d replaced it with the new-generation OM654 2.0-litre modular diesel - more efficient, more powerful, and built on an entirely new engine architecture that resolved many of the OM651's weaknesses.

milestones.description: Facelift W167; OM654 continues with mild hybrid assistance

items.title: 2.1L Twin-Turbo Diesel (2015-2019)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain stretch and guide wear - the OM651's single most critical failure point. The timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump; if it stretches beyond tolerance or a guide fails, consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth. Typical failure mileage: 75,000-120,000 miles (120,000-200,000 km).

items.commonFailure: EGR valve and cooler clogging - a known issue on OM654 engines. EGR cooler leaks have also been reported, leading to coolant loss. Typical failure mileage: 50,000-90,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 250d/300d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLE 250d's OM651 and the GLE 300d's OM654 are both fundamentally robust four-cylinder diesels, but each has well-documented weaknesses that drive replacement decisions. The OM651's timing chain is its Achilles' heel - a simplex design that stretches over time. The OM654 suffers from EGR system clogging and cooler failures that can lead to performance issues and, if ignored, more serious engine damage. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch - The W166 GLE 250d's Critical Weak Point
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a simplex timing chain design that is prone to stretching over time. The chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. If it stretches beyond tolerance or a guide fails, the consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth. Extended oil change intervals accelerate wear.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective only if addressed immediately when rattle first appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, camshaft sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: If chain rattle is present but no fault codes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2019 GLE 250d 4MATIC is worth approximately £12,000-£20,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLE 250d sits in the £8,000-£15,000 to £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start from your GLE 250d, act immediately. The OM651's timing chain is accessible with the engine in situ for tensioner and chain replacement, though gears and guides typically require more extensive work. Specialist pricing of £700-£1,200 for a full chain kit is significantly lower than dealer rates. One forum owner reported a £700 job for chain and tensioners, describing it as "not a big deal really". However, if the chain has jumped timing causing valve contact, a full replacement engine is the only safe option. On a GLE 250d worth £12,000-£20,000, a £1,000 specialist timing chain job is excellent preventative maintenance.

problems.h4: OM654 EGR Valve & Cooler Clogging - The W167 GLE 300d's Emissions Problem
problems.rootCause: The OM654's EGR system is prone to carbon build-up, particularly on vehicles used for short journeys that prevent proper regeneration cycles. The EGR cooler can also develop leaks, allowing coolant to enter the intake tract or escape externally. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation, poor performance, and check engine lights (P0401/P0402).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, clean, and decarbonise EGR valve and cooler passages
repairOptions.longevity: Restores response and fuel economy; avoid if heavily coked

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-present GLE 300d 4MATIC is worth approximately £25,000-£45,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLE 300d sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: For GLE 300d owners experiencing rough idle or hesitation, have the EGR system inspected immediately. If caught early, EGR cleaning at £200-£350 is a cost-effective solution. If the EGR cooler has failed, specialist replacement at £500-£750 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. However, if the vehicle has been driven with persistent EGR issues causing engine damage, a full rebuilt OM654 is the only safe option. Given these vehicles' high residual values, specialist replacement is almost always worth the investment.

problems.h4: OM651 Injector Failures - The Early Twin-Turbo Diesel's Other Weakness
problems.rootCause: Early OM651 engines were fitted with Delphi piezo injectors that are prone to failure. Symptoms include rough idle, limp mode, and rail pressure errors. Later magnetic-type injectors are more durable.

problems.recommendation: If you experience rough idle or limp mode on your GLE 250d, have a leak-off test performed immediately. Replacing a single faulty injector at a specialist (£250-£450) is cost-effective. However, if multiple injectors are failing, replacing all four with the later magnetic-type units (£1,000-£1,600) is the smarter long-term investment.
